@graph.name: Faecal Calprotectin Test
@graph.description: Faecal calprotectin is a neutrophil-derived protein measured in stool that reflects intestinal inflammation. It is useful for distinguishing inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) from functional bowel symptoms in appropriately selected patients, and for selected monitoring of known IBD. Elevated values do not specify a cause or prove Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis.

mainEntity.name: Can calprotectin distinguish IBS from IBD?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can help estimate likelihood of intestinal inflammation, but a final diagnosis requires clinical correlation and sometimes endoscopy.

mainEntity.name: Does a high calprotectin mean Crohn’s disease?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Crohn’s is one possible cause; infections, medicines and other inflammatory conditions may elevate it.

mainEntity.name: Does a high calprotectin mean ulcerative colitis?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. It supports intestinal inflammation but cannot identify ulcerative colitis specifically.

mainEntity.name: What is a normal calprotectin value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many assays use below 50 µg/g as a low-range result, but the reporting laboratory’s method-specific interval applies.

mainEntity.name: Does low calprotectin rule out IBD?
